top_story.headline: Immigration agency plans a $137 million no-bid deal for CoreCivic to run two New Mexico detention centers after a state law ended local detention contracts
top_story.dek: The justification says New Mexico's Immigrant Safety Act ended the local agreements that housed detainees at the Cibola and Torrance facilities, leaving CoreCivic as the only source.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement intends to award CoreCivic, Inc. a sole-source contract for detention services at the Cibola County Correctional Center and the Torrance County Detention Facility in New Mexico, according to its justification (J&A-26-0086). The document puts the estimated total cost at $136,963,356.74 for 24 months and up to 1,955 beds, with up to 980 at Cibola and 975 at Torrance. It is a single-award, indefinite-delivery contract mixing firm-fixed-price and labor-hour work. It covers housing, guards, meals, medical care and transportation for the agency's El Paso Field Office. The solicitation number is 70CDCR26R00000014.

The agency cites the 'only one responsible source' authority. The justification says New Mexico's Senate passed the Immigrant Safety Act (House Bill 9) on February 3, 2026. It quotes the law as prohibiting state and local governments from entering agreements "to detain individuals for civil immigration violations", and says the existing intergovernmental service agreements in the state were to end, with a deadline it dates to May 20, 2026. The agency's argument is that CoreCivic, the facilities' owner and operator, is the only company that can meet the requirement without a break in service.
USAspending shows CoreCivic's first federal contract on record under this name dating to June 2000. The notice was posted November 4 under the Justification type.

blocks.title: Holocaust Memorial Museum seeks a contractor for its retractable security bollards, vehicle barriers and gates in Washington and Maryland
blocks.text: The United States Holocaust Memorial Museum wants quarterly preventive maintenance, emergency service and repairs for retractable security bollards, active vehicle barriers and security gates. They are at two sites: the museum's main facility in Washington, D.C., and its Shapell Collections, Conservation and Research Center in Bowie, Maryland. The solicitation number is 95476727Q1104. Its three attachments are queued and have not yet been read.

sections.headline: Army signs off on a $419 million no-bid ceiling for Pegasystems software
paragraphs: There are 47 new sole-source justifications, 31 of them posted under other notice types, and 3 repeats from earlier editions were left out. The largest, the Immigration and Customs Enforcement deal with CoreCivic, is today's Top Story. Six extensions and bridges are in the next section.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Army gives Pegasystems a single-award software contract with a $419 million ceiling without competition
meta: only one company can do it
U.S. Army Contracting Command – Rock Island
blocks.text: The Army wants an enterprise contract for Pega software subscriptions, technical support and professional services: a five-year base ordering period plus a five-year option, with a maximum of $419,008,835.54. The justification says only Pegasystems Inc. can supply it because it owns the platform's source code, rules engine and low-code framework. It also cites Army-wide standardization and volume discounts, and rejects resellers because of pass-through markups. The contract covers renewals and previously competed Pega orders, and other Department of War components can order from it. The record flags incumbent lock-in.

blocks.title: Coast Guard buys Singapore pier services without competition for cutters evacuated from Bahrain
meta: only one company can do it
U.S. Coast Guard, Operational Logistics Command
blocks.text: The U.S. Coast Guard wants pier, berthing, office, warehouse and personnel-transport services in Singapore for up to four Fast Response Cutters from Toll Remote Logistics. The justification says all six cutters stationed in Bahrain were evacuated "following hostile enemy fire during Operation Epic Fury". They are already moored at Toll's Loyang facility under an earlier award, and the earlier pier contracts were expected to end October 21, 2026. One cutter awaits heavy repair after a catastrophic engine failure. The agency says only one pier met its security and technical needs. Toll has an earlier logged justification for pier services for six cutters (earlier notice).

blocks.title: NASA skips competition for Artemis III video recorders, citing the race with China
meta: urgent need, no time to compete
National Aeronautics and Space Administration IT Procurement Office
blocks.text: Cine Design Group LLC gets an order for Cinedeck four-channel baseband video recorders, upgrades and commissioning for Artemis III. The justification says "it is critical to the national interests of the United States ... that the Artemis program return American astronauts to the Moon before China reaches this milestone". It also cites Executive Order 14369, which sets a 2028 deadline for returning humans to the lunar surface.

blocks.title: NASA plans to lease 55 acres at Kennedy Space Center to an unnamed commercial tenant for engine testing without competition
meta: National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Kennedy Space Center
blocks.text: Posted as a Special Notice, the notice announces an intent to sole-source an Enhanced Use Lease for about 55 acres south of Schwartz Road, for second-stage and payload engine testing. NASA says a "long-standing commercial partner and tenant" showed strong interest and calls the lease "a reasonable expansion to a current tenant". The tenant is not named. Responses are due November 20, 2026, and NASA says it will use them to judge whether other parties are interested.

blocks.title: Army medical research unit plans to pay Georgia's public health center half the security bill at the Lugar Center without competition
meta: L. Sakvarelidze National Center for Disease Control and Public Health
only one company can do it
Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, Europe-Middle East
blocks.text: Posted as a Special Notice, it covers cost-share reimbursement for security services at the Richard G. Lugar Center for Public Health Research in the Republic of Georgia. The notice says the Georgian center is the "sole legal Georgian entity" that buys the security services, and the Army unit, as a co-located occupant that is not a Georgian legal entity, cannot contract for them itself. The implementing agreement has the Army unit paying a share of the Lugar Center's operating cost (the notice text gives 50%). Capability statements are due by 2:00 p.m. Eastern on November 23, 2026.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Defense Information Systems Agency keeps its Fort Meade building contractor through a no-bid bridge
paragraphs: Six new extensions or bridges: two bridge and extension contracts at a defense agency and NASA, plus smaller renewals.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency bridges GCR-Dean's building operations contract at its Fort Meade headquarters without competition
meta: only one company can do it
blocks.text: The bridge keeps GCR-Dean, LLC running building operations at the agency's 1.07-million-square-foot Fort Meade headquarters, which houses a network operations center, IT labs and extensive secure-room space. The agency says the follow-on contract cannot be awarded and transitioned before the current task order expires. The document lists the incumbent's prior contract as running May 2, 2021 to November 1, 2026, after earlier competed contracts back to 2010. The length of the bridge is not given. GCR-Dean has an earlier logged sole-source justification for base operations support (earlier notice).

blocks.title: NASA extends HX5 Sierra's Glenn test-facility contract without competition at $13.3 million for three months of estimates
meta: only one company can do it
National Aeronautics and Space Administration, Glenn Research Center
blocks.text: The extension keeps HX5 Sierra, LLC running test-facility operations, maintenance and engineering services at the National Aeronautics and Space Administration's Glenn Research Center. The justification says the company's January, February and March estimates total $13,297,737. The agency says HX5 Sierra's "years of previous experience" at the center's test facilities, with specialized equipment and test procedures, make it the only responsible source for the interim period.

sections.headline: Army Corps of Engineers will build a Cyber Operations Center at Lackland through an Other Transaction agreement
paragraphs: There are 265 new solicitations, with 95 repeats left out. Twenty-five were flagged, and most of those were already listed or are false alarms.

blocks.title: Army Corps of Engineers seeks a design-build team for a $-undisclosed 42,000-square-foot Air Force cyber operations center in Texas
meta: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Fort Worth District
blocks.text: On behalf of the Air Force, the Fort Worth District seeks a design-build team for the 91st Cyber Operations Center at Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland. It is an approximately 42,000-square-foot, multi-story facility for the Air Combat Command's 91st Cyber Operations Squadron. The delivery model is a Progressive Design-Build agreement under Other Transaction authority (10 U.S.C. § 2808a), which falls outside the Federal Acquisition Regulation. Five attachments are queued and have not been read.

blocks.text: The multiple-award, indefinite-delivery contracts would cover design-build and construction nationwide. There would be three pools set aside for service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses and one national unrestricted pool, each with at least ten awardees. footer.known_gaps: No source errors were reported. OMB apportionments: no flagged or specially conditioned files in the window. Of 2,284 attachments on 489 SAM.gov notices, about 608 have been read, including earlier runs. 1,601 are queued for later editions, 72 are access-restricted on SAM.gov and 3 could not be downloaded or read; 10,148 files in all are queued for later editions. About 1,241 links to outside portals (mostly DLA DIBBS and PIEE) were not followed. The Defense Health Agency traumatic brain injury forum justification was judged from the notice blurb only.
